subject: Nonstandard pack cushion credit request — exec endorsement
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@biometrics.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: procure@biometrics.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question + cushion credit for pilot

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profile looks promising for our patient-facing workflows. We're close to signing the pilot SOW but ran into an internal procurement issue: our usage pattern is spiky (long tail of small bursts across many endpoints) and the standard up-front packages overweight committed tokens.

Procurement asked whether Redwood can offer a short-term "cushion" credit to smooth the first 90 days so we don't hit overage charges while we tune prompts and caching. They also want a hybrid tier (a small committed baseline + a burst pool billed at lower per-token rate). Can you confirm if this is possible and what approvals we'd need?

Attached is a draft SOW and a quick traffic sample. We need an answer by Friday to keep internal momentum.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Product
BioMetrics AI

Attachments: biometrics_sow_v2.pdf (application/pdf), traffic_sample.csv (text/csv)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@biometrics.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question + cushion credit for pilot

Elena — appreciate the context and the file. Happy to keep momentum. Short answer: yes, we can do a 90-day cushion credit + a hybrid baseline/burst structure, but anything outside standard packaging needs VP/CFO sign-off.

Proposal I discussed with Sales Ops:
- 90-day cushion credit equivalent to 10% of estimated pilot spend (one-time credit applied to first invoice).
- Baseline: small committed monthly token block priced at standard pilot rate.
- Burst pool: separate meter with a reduced per-token rate vs. standard overage to absorb spikes for first 90 days.

Why this helps: removes friction for Procurement, preserves unit economics by limiting total exposure, and gives us telemetry to recommend a long-term tier.

I'm copying Marissa (VP, Sales) and Markus (Finance) to request an exception memo and sign-off. Marissa — short ask: can you approve the structure in principle and escalate to Markus for CFO authorization? If helpful I can attach a quick expected P&L delta (two-slide) and the customer's traffic sample.

Next steps: Elena, if you confirm the expected pilot budget range (ballpark monthly spend), I'll kick off an internal memo for exec approval.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_model_biometrics.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Nonstandard pack cushion credit request — exec endorsement

Markus — quick background: BioMetrics is a high-velocity health-tech prospect with strong expansion potential if pilot succeeds. Dylan outlined a conservative structure: 90-day cushion credit (10% of pilot spend) + hybrid baseline + burst pool with reduced overage. The customer's ask is narrow and time-bound; procurement wants confirmatory language in the SOW.

Business case in 2 bullets:
- Near-term revenue hit from the credit is small relative to expected ARR if they convert (they've signaled interest in a 12–18 month roll once pilot proves OOS).
- The burst pool reduces ops churn early and should materially lower support/latency tuning effort for them — increasing likelihood of conversion.

Request: Finance sign-off to permit a one-time credit up to 10% and authorization to include the hybrid burst pricing for a defined 90-day window. If you prefer, I can present this at Monday's commercial approvals meeting; otherwise a reply here suffices.

I attached a 2-slide impact summary.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: memos/biometrics_impact_summary_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, Elena Morales <elena@biometrics.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nonstandard pack cushion credit request — exec endorsement

Thanks for the summary — I reviewed the attached model and traffic sample. I'm comfortable authorizing the exception with conditions:

1) Credit capped at 10% of the agreed pilot value and applied only to the first invoice.
2) The hybrid burst pool must have a strict upper bound charge (hard cap) equal to 40% above baseline expected usage; any consumption beyond that will revert to standard overage pricing and requires an escalation.
3) SOW must include telemetry milestone at day 60 with agreed success criteria (latency < 250ms p95 on representative sample) — if milestone is missed, we reserve right to reprice or terminate pilot.

If Dylan can update the SOW language with these conditions, I approve. Please capture the approval in the deal record (HubSpot deal 4821) and include the final SOW link when you send to Elena.

Markus Klein
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference

[Signed electronically]

CC: procurement@biometrics.ai — attaching for visibility.
